answers.answer: For a recurring message: open Triggers and timers in the sidebar and the Timers tab, choose New timer, type a Name, keep Reaction on Simple reply, type one message per line in Messages, keep Twitch chat under Send the reply to, set Minutes between posts (default 30), then choose Create timer. To answer a chat phrase: open the Chat triggers tab, choose New trigger, type the Words to watch for and the Reply, keep Twitch chat, then choose Create trigger. Each list step names its control, and I could do every step in order.
answers.quote: Open Triggers and timers in the sidebar, then the Timers tab.

answers.answer: You need the Moderator, Lead moderator, Editor or Broadcaster role to open the page and make changes. A VIP can only view the tabs, and only when the Broadcaster opens the views to VIPs. This is stated in Who can use this page, before the first steps.
answers.quote: A Moderator, Lead moderator, Editor or Broadcaster may open the page and change timers and chat triggers.

answers.answer: Success: the dialog closes and the new timer or trigger shows in the list, switched on. A wrong field stops the dialog with a red reason, and the page lists the exact texts. The two concepts differ by what starts them: a timer waits for time and, optionally, chat activity; a chat trigger watches ordinary messages for chosen words. A command is a separate thing that starts with the prefix.
answers.quote: The dialog closes and the new timer shows in the list, switched on.

answers.answer: A reminder saved before going live posts nothing while offline. Going live starts a fresh time count, so the first post comes one full Minutes between posts after the stream starts (30 minutes by default). A new timer has Chat lines needed at 0, so it posts at the next check, within about 30 seconds of that point. It stops posting when the stream ends but stays saved, because timers run only while the channel is live. It does not need to be remade.
answers.quote: Going live starts a fresh time count: the first line of a stream waits one full Minutes between posts.

answers.answer: The paragraphs about a Duplicate copy's timing sit in When a timer posts, before the page explains Duplicate in Edit a timer. There I read 'Switch the copy on' before I learned that a copy starts switched off, and I had to jump ahead to understand it. I also had to guess whether pausing a timer from the quick actions on Home is the same state as the Enabled switch marked Off. The page describes both but does not link them. Cost: a short detour and one small guess. No step was blocked.
answers.quote: A copy made with Duplicate keeps the Chat lines needed of the timer it copies.

answers.answer: 'Holds the whole channel' is an odd way to say the cooldown applies to everyone in the channel; a listener has to work it out. The detailed check rules for a duplicated timer (two numbered conditions, counted since the bot began watching) are dense when read aloud. Most readers will not act on them. Cost: a moment of confusion, not a blocked task.
answers.quote: Seconds between replies holds the whole channel.
